description: I am a driven problem solver and a proud member of Team Quantum Leapers, participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Passionate about Earth observation and the power of collaborative technology, I am helping our team bridge critical data gaps by harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS satellite data.
summary:
UAE Fire Tracker is a web-based application designed to visualize and monitor fire hotspot activity across the United Arab Emirates. It provides an interactive dashboard that displays fire-related data through charts, statistics, and geographical maps.

The project uses MODIS and VIIRS satellite data formats and allows users to explore fire activity across different years, analyze trends, and view hotspot locations.
details:
Our project harmonizes active fire and thermal anomaly detections from NASA's MODIS (1 km resolution) and VIIRS (375 m resolution) satellite sensors across the United Arab Emirates (2022–2026) into a unified "Burning Calendar" dashboard. Because VIIRS has a much finer spatial resolution than MODIS, raw counts make fire activity look artificially higher after VIIRS launched. We solve this by snapping both datasets onto a common spatial grid, deduplicating overlapping detections per day, and comparing daily Fire Radiative Power (FRP) and active grid cells against a multi-year historical baseline.

Benefits & intended impact:

Local environmental and emergency teams in the UAE often deal with false alarms from static industrial gas flaring (such as Ruwais and Habshan) alongside genuine agricultural and brush fires in regions like Al Ain, Ras Al Khaimah, and Fujairah. Our tool lets users filter confidence thresholds, separate true thermal anomalies from baseline industrial heat, and spot unusual seasonal fire spikes at a glance.

Tools, languages & resources used:

We built the web app using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, integrating the NASA FIRMS API (MODIS_NRT and VIIRS_NOAA20_NRT), Apache ECharts for the calendar heatmap and baseline trend charts, and Leaflet with CARTO Voyager basemap tiles for geospatial mapping. We hosted the open-source codebase and live application on GitHub Pages.
